answer: An agent economy can bind voting power to a unique human credential issued after an in-person proof-of-personhood check, then let each credential authorize only one agent at a time. This makes spinning up a thousand falcon accounts useless: they still carry one person’s weight. The attacker must recruit or impersonate many people and repeat the checks, paying in time, coordination and exposure. A velvet interface may ease honest onboarding, but the credential remains the anchor against cheap identities.
